title: Fixed points of nonexpansive maps
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's solution (2026) of Kirk's problem: every nonexpansive self-map of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point, for the given norm. The first lesson proves weak compactness in reflexive spaces, limits along an ultrafilter, the reduction to a minimal invariant set of diameter 1 with metrizable weak topology, the Goebel-Karlovitz diametral lemma, Kirk's normal-structure theorem and a compact detector lemma. The second constructs resolvents, a family of maps with controlled displacement, the pointwise weak topology, Ellis's idempotent lemma, an anchor point in the closed convex hull of its tail images, and an adaptive selection with prescribed precision. The third builds an infinite ordered tree of maps with budgets and functionals, choosing each functional against a compact family of predicted root outputs. The fourth switches leaves to a common approximate fixed point, detects every block, finds a common witness along a branch, and derives the contradiction.
prerequisites: foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras lesson hahn-banach-baire-and-the-basic-theorems-on-banach-spaces (Theorem 1.1 Zorn; Corollary 2.3 Hahn-Banach; Theorem 4.2 uniform boundedness; Theorem 6.3 strict separation); lesson weak-topologies-tychonoff-banach-alaoglu-mazur-bipolars-krein-milman-and-eberlein-smulian (Theorem 2.3 Tychonoff; Theorem 3.1 Banach-Alaoglu; Theorem 4.1 Mazur)
tingleys-problem lesson ultrapowers-and-darbos-fixed-point-theorem (Lemma 1.1, free ultrafilters on N)
